conceptual_explanation: Level 5 Relative Mastery focuses on 'Relative Clauses of Quantity' and using 'Which' to describe an entire situation. These structures are extremely common in academic writing and high-level reports.

rule_cards.name: Relative Clauses of Quantity
rule_cards.correct: There were 20 guests, ten of whom were students.
rule_cards.incorrect: There were 20 guests, ten of them were students. (Comma Splice)

rule_cards.name: The Clause-Modifying 'Which'
rule_cards.correct: He arrived late, which annoyed the teacher.
rule_cards.incorrect: He arrived late, that annoyed the teacher.

rule_cards.name: Prepositional Formalism
rule_cards.correct: The conditions under which they worked were harsh.
rule_cards.incorrect: The conditions which they worked under...

rule_cards.name: Object-Subject Trap
rule_cards.formula: The man whom [I thought] was... (Error check)
rule_cards.correct: The man who I thought was the thief turned out to be innocent.
rule_cards.incorrect: The man whom I thought was the thief... (If 'who' is the subject of 'was')

head_noun_tasks.explanation: 'Three of whom' is a relative clause of quantity modifying 'directors'.
'Which' refers back to the entire situation of her failing the test.
'In which' modifies 'manner' in a formal prepositional structure.
'Most of which' is a relative clause of quantity modifying 'gifts'.
'To which' is a formal prepositional structure modifying 'extent'.

drill_tasks.question: He presented three options, ________ were feasible.
drill_tasks.explanation: Use a relative pronoun (which) to connect the clause; 'none of them' would cause a comma splice.

drill_tasks.question: The speed ________ the car was traveling was dangerous.
drill_tasks.explanation: We say 'at a speed', so the formal relative is 'at which'.

drill_tasks.question: The witness, ________ I believed was telling the truth, suddenly became nervous.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'was telling the truth'; 'I believed' is a parenthetical insertion.

drill_tasks.question: He lost his job, ________ came as a shock to his family.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'Which' can refer to the entire preceding clause.

drill_tasks.question: We have fifty employees, ________ are under thirty.
drill_tasks.explanation: Relative clause of quantity for people.

boss_fight.paragraph: I have two sisters, both of them are doctors. He broke the window, that was very careless. The way how he speaks is annoying.

errors.explanation: To connect two clauses with a comma, you must use a relative pronoun ('whom'), not a personal pronoun ('them').
'That' cannot be used in non-defining clauses or to refer to a whole clause; use 'which'.
Never use 'way how'. Use 'the way' alone, or 'the way in which'.

success_feedback: Impressive! You've navigated the complexities of quantitative and clause-modifying relatives. Your precision is truly high-level.
suggested_next_steps: Practice using 'at which', 'to which', and 'in which' in formal writing.
Try using 'some of whom' to describe a group of people.
